prediction_scored: hit: the registered range for speed was +5% to +15% and the estimate is +5.7% (+2.9 to +8.6); the registered range for trips was -3% to -12% and the estimate is -9.8% (-12.8 to -6.6). The trip result is weaker than it looks, because the 2024 placebo also shows a CBD decline (-4.5%, -6.3 to -2.7), so about half of it is a pre-existing trend.
settle: The speed result is settled in direction. Its size needs a longer post-period (the MTA speed series ends in August 2025) and a comparison that is not affected by diverted traffic, for example speeds on comparable streets in other large US cities. Trip counts need a model with area-specific trends.

notes: Speeds rose in the CBD relative to Greater NYC by the registered amount, and the 2024 placebo for speed is null (-0.8%). Against the CBD-adjacent area the effect is +4.2%. By industry, high-volume FHV trips in the CBD fell -14.3% relative to outside and yellow taxi trips -4.7%; green cabs, which rarely serve the CBD, show no change. The MTA CBD vehicle-miles series (jbxx-kxff) shows 2025 CRZ daily VMT -3.8% (AGPS measure) and -11.0% (connected-vehicle measure) against the same months of 2024, without a comparison area. TLC trips are exposure to the policy as well as a measure of traffic, because the per-trip CBD surcharge falls on them directly.
